en: Can we get a table for four, please?
tamil: நாலு பேருக்கு ஒரு டேபிள் கிடைக்குமா, please?
context: Asking the host for a table when you arrive.
explain: 'Can we get' is a polite way to ask for something. Add 'please' to sound friendly.

alt.en: Could we have a table for four?
alt.tamil: நாலு பேருக்கு ஒரு டேபிள் தர முடியுமா?

en: Do you have a table near the window?
context: Asking for a nicer seat at a restaurant.
explain: Use 'Do you have' to ask if something is available. 'Near' tells the place.

en: We have a reservation under the name Kumar.
tamil: எங்க பேர்ல ஒரு ரிசர்வேஷன் இருக்கு, குமார்னு.
context: Telling the host you booked a table already.
explain: 'Under the name' is the normal way to give the booking name.

en: I booked a table for eight o'clock.
tamil: நான் எட்டு மணிக்கு ஒரு டேபிள் புக் பண்ணிருந்தேன்.
context: Confirming your booking at the entrance.
explain: 'Booked' is the past of 'book'. We say 'for' plus the time.

alt.en: I made a booking for eight tonight.
alt.tamil: நான் இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி எட்டு மணிக்கு புக்கிங் பண்ணிருந்தேன்.

en: May we have the menu, please?
context: Asking the waiter for the menu card.
explain: 'Could' is softer and more polite than 'can'.

en: What do you recommend here?
context: Asking the waiter for his suggestion.
explain: 'Recommend' means to suggest something good. Use 'What do you...' to ask for an opinion.

en: I'll have the masala dosa and a filter coffee.
tamil: நான் மசாலா தோசையும் ஒரு ஃபில்டர் காபியும் சாப்பிடுறேன்.
context: Placing your order with the waiter.
explain: 'I'll have' is the common way to order food. It decides your order right now.

en: Is this dish very spicy?
context: Checking the spice level before ordering.
explain: Start with 'Is' to ask about a quality. 'Very' adds strength.

en: Please make it less spicy.
context: Asking the cook to reduce chilli.
explain: 'Make it' plus an adjective changes how food is prepared. 'Please' keeps it polite.

alt.en: Could you make it mild, please?

en: I'm allergic to nuts, so could you check if this has any?
tamil: எனக்கு நட்ஸ் அலர்ஜி, அதனால இதுல இருக்கான்னு பார்க்க முடியுமா?
context: Telling the waiter about an allergy politely.
explain: 'Allergic to' is followed by the food. 'So' gives the reason for your request.

en: We're still deciding, so please give us a few more minutes.
tamil: நாங்க இன்னும் முடிவு பண்ணல, கொஞ்ச நேரம் கொடுங்க please.
context: When the waiter comes before you are ready.
explain: Use present continuous for something happening now. 'A few more minutes' asks for a little time.

en: Do you have any vegetarian options?
context: Asking about meatless dishes.
explain: We use 'any' in questions. 'Options' means the choices on the menu.

en: I don't eat meat, but I do eat eggs.
tamil: நான் இறைச்சி சாப்பிட மாட்டேன், ஆனா முட்டை சாப்பிடுவேன்.
context: Explaining your food habits to a host.
explain: 'Do eat' adds a little stress to show the contrast with the first part.

en: The soup is a bit too salty for me.
tamil: சூப் எனக்கு கொஞ்சம் உப்பு அதிகமா இருக்கு.
context: Giving a gentle complaint about taste.
explain: 'A bit too' is a soft way to say something is more than you like.

en: This biryani is really tasty!
tamil: இந்த பிரியாணி உண்மையிலேயே ரொம்ப ருசியா இருக்கு!
context: Praising the food while eating.
explain: 'Really' makes the adjective stronger. 'Tasty' is a simple word for good-tasting food.

en: Could I get some more water, please?
context: Asking the waiter for water.
explain: 'Some more' means an extra amount. 'Could I get' is polite.

en: We haven't ordered yet.
context: Telling the waiter you are not ready.
explain: Use 'haven't' plus a past form with 'yet' for something not done till now.

en: My order hasn't come yet. Could you check?
tamil: என் ஆர்டர் இன்னும் வரல. கொஞ்சம் பார்க்க முடியுமா?
context: When your food is late.
explain: 'Hasn't come yet' shows something expected is still missing. End with a polite request.

en: Could we have the bill, please?
context: Asking for the bill at the end of a meal.
explain: 'Have the bill' is the usual phrase. It is polite and short.

alt.en: Can you bring the bill, please?

en: Can we split the bill?
context: Paying separately with friends.
explain: 'Split' means to divide something between people.

en: Do you accept UPI payments?
context: Asking how you can pay.
explain: 'Accept' means to take something offered. Use it for payment methods.

en: Is the service charge already included in the bill?
context: Checking the final amount.
explain: 'Already included' means it is part of the amount. Use 'Is' with a singular noun.

en: I'll pay by card.
context: Telling the cashier how you will pay.
explain: 'Pay by' is followed by the method, like card or cash. 'I'll' shows a quick decision.

en: Please keep the change.
context: Leaving a small tip for the waiter.
explain: 'Keep the change' is a friendly way to give a tip.

en: The food was delicious, thank you.
context: Thanking the staff when you leave.
explain: 'Was' is the past of 'is'. Add 'thank you' to be polite.

en: We waited for forty minutes for our food.
context: Complaining about slow service.
explain: 'Waited for' is used with the thing you wait for. 'Waited' is past tense.

en: I didn't order this dish.
context: When the wrong item arrives.
explain: 'Didn't' plus the base verb makes a past negative.

en: Could you pack the rest for takeaway?
context: Taking leftover food home.
explain: 'Pack' means to put in a box or bag. 'The rest' means the remaining food.

en: I'm going to try the chicken curry today.
tamil: நான் இன்னைக்கு சிக்கன் கறி சாப்பிட்டு பார்க்கப் போறேன்.
context: Deciding what to eat.
explain: 'Going to' shows a plan you have decided. 'Try' means to taste something new.

en: Have you ever eaten at this restaurant?
context: Asking a friend about their experience.
explain: 'Have you ever' asks about experience in your life. 'Eaten' is the past participle of 'eat'.

en: I've already eaten, so I'll just have tea.
tamil: நான் ஏற்கனவே சாப்பிட்டுட்டேன், அதனால டீ மட்டும் குடிப்பேன்.
context: Joining friends at a restaurant when not hungry.
explain: 'Already' goes between 'have' and the past participle.

en: What time does the kitchen close?
context: Checking if you can still order.
explain: Use 'does' with 'he/she/it' subjects in questions. The verb stays in base form.

en: I would like to cancel my reservation for tonight.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரிக்கான என் ரிசர்வேஷனை கேன்சல் பண்ணணும்.
context: Calling the restaurant to cancel.
explain: 'I would like to' is a polite way to say what you want.

en: Can I change my booking to Saturday evening?
context: Calling to move your table.
explain: 'Change to' tells the new time. 'Can I' asks for permission.

en: My mother makes the best sambar.
context: Talking about home cooking with friends.
explain: 'The best' is the top level. Use present simple for general facts.

en: I cook rice and dal almost every day.
tamil: நான் கிட்டத்தட்ட தினமும் சாதமும் பருப்பும் சமைப்பேன்.
context: Describing your cooking habit.
explain: Present simple shows habits. 'Almost every day' means very often.

en: I was cooking dinner when you called.
tamil: நீங்க கூப்பிட்டப்போ நான் ராத்திரி சாப்பாடு சமைச்சுக்கிட்டு இருந்தேன்.
context: Explaining why you missed a call.
explain: Use 'was cooking' for a longer action and 'called' for the short action that interrupted it.

en: Add a little salt and stir well.
context: Giving a simple cooking instruction.
explain: Recipes use the base verb for instructions. 'A little' means a small amount.

en: Let the onions turn golden before you add the tomatoes.
tamil: தக்காளி போடுறதுக்கு முன்னாடி வெங்காயம் பொன்னிறமா ஆகட்டும்.
context: Explaining a cooking step.
explain: 'Let' plus an object and base verb gives an instruction. 'Before' links two steps.

en: She is making chapatis in the kitchen right now.
tamil: அவங்க இப்போ கிச்சன்ல சப்பாத்தி செஞ்சுக்கிட்டு இருக்காங்க.
context: Saying what someone is doing at this moment.
explain: 'Is making' shows an action in progress. 'Right now' stresses the moment.

en: I never put sugar in my coffee.
context: Telling how you take your drink.
explain: 'Never' goes before the main verb and means not at any time.

en: We'll cook something simple tonight.
context: Planning dinner at home.
explain: 'We'll' is short for 'we will'. 'Something simple' means an easy meal.
